Masterserver: the logs of every relayed signalling message come at most once in 10 seconds each. Every peer may relay 20 messages a second, so with thousands of peers these lines alone could fill the disk.

Nicknames and server names may contain no control characters (C0 and DEL) - before, only the null character and whitespace other than space were refused, so a server name with terminal escape sequences got into the masterserver's log and every player's server browser. The masterserver also strips them from the WebRTC id a peer asks for, and logs the destination id of a relayed message only once it resolved to a registered peer - a JSON string escape in it could forge log lines.

Masterserver: tell_me_my_address is answered at most 50 times a second (bursts of 100) per network and 2000 times a second in all. Anyone can send it, and the answer goes to the packet's source address - spoofed sources could bounce a flood of answers off the masterserver at a victim, each also logged. Limited per network (augs::network_of), as per ip:port a new port for every packet would get past it; the table of networks is bounded by clearing it when full, which is why there is also the limit on all answers. NAT detection asks far less often than that. The answer is still about twice the size of the request - padding the request (a protocol change) would remove the amplification entirely.
chore(web): Ever Platform SDK 1.0.0-rc.7

Masterserver: at most 4096 signalling messages wait to be relayed to native endpoints. The queue had no bound - every peer relaying towards native servers grew it faster than it drains, up to the memory. A message is resent over half a second anyway, so with a full queue new ones are dropped.

Masterserver: web servers' signalling messages and all heartbeats are rate-limited. Anyone can make their WebSocket session a server with one heartbeat signed with their own key, and a server's messages were not limited at all - one session could flood other peers and listed native servers through the relay. Now a server gets ten times a client's allowance (200 messages a second, bursts of 1000) instead of an unlimited one. Heartbeats cost a token too: one changing a field every time made the main thread rewrite the whole list up to the WebSocket's throughput, and each was logged (now at most once in 10 seconds). Only a registered peer relays - one refused for too many peers could still relay with an empty source id.

Masterserver: the main thread is given only the web servers, and only what the list shows of them (signalling_peer_listing, get_new_servers_map). Before, every list refresh copied the whole peer map under the peers' lock - thousands of clients with their sockets and received-guid sets - and previous_peers kept those sockets alive until the next refresh. The new-server webhook fires as before: for a peer not a server at the previous refresh.
